title: The Senses as Rooms; The First Lifespan
description: T57 describes the body as a vessel formed by self-claiming yet bearing the divine pattern. Within this molded body the proprium has set up faculties for each sense, each with its own house, storehouses, and inner chambers. Whatever the eye sees is carried inward and laid up in those storehouses; whatever the ear hears is deposited and watched over. Above all five sits the heart, ruling as a king before whom the senators of his city stand — and the body is an encampment with gates, the gates being the senses. The Lord ordering the rational comes to take the keys. T58 explains why what the soul once bore in fullness comes forth now small and feeble: there are five orders of governance (year, month, day, hour, moment) and as each shrinks in turn, what is brought forth grows smaller — the wide ordering ruled at the beginning, narrowing as the soul moves through formation.
